**Reproduced teaching shortcut.** The intended rule is simultaneous one-row motion based on the original input. A plausible rival performs a mutable bottom-up sweep: lower cells move first, and an upper cell may then enter a location vacated earlier in the same sweep.

Across 40 seeds × 18 three-demo starts per difficulty, this rival survived 2/720 easy windows and 0/720 windows in each of the default, medium, and hard bands (`checks/audit/e873f4e123b6/scan_summary.json`). The exact emitted witness is easy seed 36: demos at sample indices 15–17 all fit the rival, while query sample 18 separates it. All four inputs came directly from `generate()` and the target declares no `self_check`, so this is inside the produced domain.

The complete grids and outputs are in `checks/audit/e873f4e123b6/witness.json`. Canonical Racket was executed with rule hash `b42ab5510ab4`; the three demo outputs equal the rival outputs, while the query differs. This is not merely an outside-domain thought experiment.

**Suggested repair.** Declare the bottom-up rival and ensure every three-demo window contains a vertical chain where a lower member can move but the upper member must stay under simultaneous semantics. A small lesson-window regression should enumerate schedule residues rather than relying only on aggregate vertical-adjacency frequency.
